institutionName: UiT The Arctic University of Norway

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I love norway, and i wanted to try something different then denmark, thats why i took as long north as i could. i didnt know much about tromsø so i wanted an adventure

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I liked my study abroad experience a lot, it was a good experince to try something new and to meet new people. the classes were also very exiting and i got to learn something new. i will never forget it.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It took some time to get to know everything and to find the informtion i needed. but at the end i got it, and i could also talk to the student help service, so i think it took some effort but in the end it worked out.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: mobility supervisor and host university supervisor helped me. i went up and talked to them.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: it was very satisfactory and people were nice.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: pretty easy, i used samskipnaden website to get a house.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: There are good facilitations, with sauna and shared kitchen. future students should now samskipnaden, which maybe is on campus, maybe i have confused that.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I think the housing was very nice, good kitchen, sauna and stuff like that.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: it took some time, there is a lot of emails, and mobility work to do, and also a lot og documents

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: through mobility i got to know how to connect with the host university through emails, and they also had a website i used to get courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: mobility supervisor and host university supervisor, and also the mobility superviser at my home university

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: i got all 3, and those were the ones i wanted, and it also matched up pretty well, so i am going to finish my bachelor in 3 years.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: check mobility often, and try to find courses that match the courses in your student plan, if they dont have courses that match the student plan, you should consider going to another university, or else it will get complicated and you will have to finish your bachelor later then expected probably

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: i think it was very well, i learned a lot. the teaching methods and courses were a bit different than what i was used to at my home university, but that was a challenge but i learned a lot.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It was different the teaching, and some i think were a little above my home iuniversyty. especially microbiology, there was a lot there that i wasnt used to. but it worked out.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: it was a little different. there were more reports and assingments and tours to the sea.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: marine ecology, ocean climate and microbiology

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: ocean climate and marine ecology. microbiology in norwegian is difficult for a danish student because of the language and also because of the level i think, at least if you like me study natural ressources and not biochemistry

questions.answer: very good opportunites for going to sports and clubs and nightlife

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: sports and waffle friday

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: sports and waffle friday is a good way to meet other students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: go hiking, and hang out with friends, see the museums

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: the norwegian and danish barrier was a little difficult, but overall it went okay, and if you are good at english it is fine.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: do sports and waffle friday

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: the language barrier between danish and norwegian

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: the hiking

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: go hiking and go do sports, and select the right courses

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: pick a good housing and take the right courses

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: the hiking and being somewhere else and meeting new people

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: in the beginning and socialising and adjusting to all the new. the new courses were different

questions.answer: no
